No exact publication date, individual authors, persistent DOI, or reuse license was identified. Synthetic and real-matrix results are not interchangeable; reference-only and not a GreenHub default. Retrieved 2026-11-06.

source_notes: 120 treatment-by-site-by-month records from 10 sites. Source values are g dry matter/m2; one biomass value is missing. Measurements are standing biomass snapshots, not delivered or annual harvested yield. Zenodo confirms version DOI 15349657 and concept DOI 15349656. Reference-only; do not apply as direct Pareto feed availability. Exact Zenodo Biomass.csv and Analysis.R are now preserved in the linked source subfolder with verified Zenodo MD5 and local SHA-256. The root-level semicolon CSV remains for compatibility; parsed values match, with line endings normalized.

Announcement dated 7 January 2025 says the permitted plant can process up to 60,000 t/year of plant-based raw materials. Design/permit capacity, not realized throughput. No raw-feed basis or availability measurement is provided.

Approximate 600 t announcement; exact publication timestamp, weighing records, mass basis and source locations are not supplied. The associated project-agenda event is dated 2025-11-07. Do not treat as measured delivered supply or runtime availability.

Article and dataset identifiers are distinct: article DOI 10.1111/avsc.70085; Zenodo dataset version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15349657 (CC BY 4.0). The article license is CC BY-NC. The 2023 values are standing biomass, not annual harvested or delivered supply. No runtime/default activation.

Article reports 334 pesticide-residue detections, mean 0.0645 mg/kg among detected residues, and LOQ 0.01 mg/kg fresh weight. The GreenHub proxy is a lower-bound average derived by setting nondetections to zero and transferring from South Tyrol public grass to Dutch roadside grass. It is not a VARTA measurement or compliance result. Underlying data record: https://zenodo.org/records/7357488; article is CC BY 4.0, separate raw-data license not stated in the reviewed record.

CC BY 4.0 per institutional bibliography record. Table 2 and Sections 2.1–2.5, 3.3–3.5 report derived estimates based on county road/mowing information and visually screened 2024 orthophotography. Not a Dutch seasonal feed profile, measured delivered supply, or GreenHub runtime input; reference-only.

CC BY 4.0. Table 2 reports a 9,931 t wet-matter total across 41 collection points; Scenario 1 reports 9,841 t. These are planning estimates, not weighbridge measurements or GreenHub supply; reference-only with no runtime mapping.

Catalogue description reports 76,084 t/year; the linked provincial WFS records sum to 90,321 t/year. Keep the source-version discrepancy visible; the stream is mixed municipal green waste and cannot be interpreted as roadside-grass supply.

Chapter 3, §§3.2.1–3.2.3, pp. 10–11. Reports approximate annual collected/processed and uncollected quantities and a typical twice-yearly mowing schedule; no mass basis or underlying metering method is supplied. The report is dated 05 June 2015. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified. Regional project estimates are context only, not GreenHub feedstock defaults.
Current guidance reports approximate weeks for first/second ecological rounds and separate safety-strip mowing; not a biomass availability profile. No explicit reuse license identified.

DataverseNO dataset DOI 10.18710/F5Z8BR (CC0 1.0); related article DOI 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2025.180373. 192 treatment-summary rows and 8 experiment-location rows; source README defines yield as g/m² dry matter and nitrogen-rate codes, but does not define CP/clover column units. Values are pooled/averaged summaries, not raw replicates. Reference-only: not roadside grass, GreenHub supply, or a runtime default.

Describes process sequence and exploratory product routes but publishes no unit-level quantities, mass balances, recovery, chemistry, energy, costs, or emissions. The grass-juice-to-biogas route was under investigation. Reference-only.

Draft calendar and regional context are not measured monthly GreenHub availability. Source quality varies by statement; approximate press-yield/process commentary remains proxy-level and must not set default seasonal mass.

Homepage section lists 36,000 t verge grass and 24,000 t vegetable residues, plus biomethane, liquid bio-CO2, green fertilizer and substrate quantities. Product-target period, analytical specifications and operational measurement basis are not stated. Treat as project targets, not performance measurements.

Homepage states up to 30,000 t/year roadside cuttings within 3–5 years; approach page states 30,000 t/year biogenic residuals including public-space and horticultural sources. These are ambitions, not measured capacity or throughput. Feed basis, hours, commissioning, contracts, and realized supply are unstated. Do not add the values or equate the scopes. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified.

J-STAGE abstract reports glucose 1.0–4.4%, fructose 0.7–5.0%, sucrose 0.3–4.5%, fructosan 1.2–12.6%, and total NSC 4.2–21.8% of DM. Methods: 80% ethanol extraction/LC for mono- and disaccharides, hot-water extraction/anthrone for fructosan. Ranges have no reported replicate count, SD, or stage-specific values in the abstract. Used only as allocation weights within a separate Smit roadside-grass total; resulting GreenHub values are class-C proxies, not measurements. Reuse license not identified; verify before redistribution beyond this project.

Layer energie:RESTSTROMEN_GROENAFVAL; property GEMEENTELIJK_GROENAFVAL_TON; JAAR=2022. Retrieved WFS total is 90,321 t/year while catalog description reports 76,084 t/year; preserve discrepancy. No roadside-grass fraction, dry/wet basis or GreenHub allocation. Public-domain metadata; reference-only.

Main report states approximately 11,000 t/year across four parcels. Appendix reports parcel areas, 1,500 t for East, approximately 2,500 t for West, and an explicitly estimated 3,500 t/year for South because primary data were unavailable. Appendix separately calculates theoretical fresh-biomass potential from a literature yield factor. Tonnes for contractor/provincial amounts have no wet/dry basis or underlying weighbridge tickets; possible ditch material is noted. North parcel quantity not inferred. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified.

Numerical table transcribed from Pacheco and Waghorn (2008), Table 3, p.110, which attributes it to this primary study. Values are nitrogen-basis percentages; rows do not sum to 100%. Reference-only and not a GreenHub species-mass allocation.
Official BDB report commissioned by OVAM; field observations and literature synthesis. DOI not identified; do not infer an annual GreenHub supply value.
Official page reports more than 18,000 ha of motorway verges and usually one annual mowing; area is not all grass or recoverable feedstock.
Only values explicitly visible in accessible abstract were eligible.

Original Dutch workbook retained locally; English fibre and juice extracts preserve source sheet and row. No DOI or external reuse license. GreenHub whole-grass and juice rows are not proven to be the same batch; no press inlet/outlet masses or seasonal supply are given.

Page reports approximately 10,000 tonnes of verge grass mown per year, two mowing rounds (June–July and September–October), and collection after a short field-rest period. Article publication date and mass basis are not stated; not a contracted GreenHub supply figure. No DOI or persistent article identifier identified; local source_id is used for repository linkage.

Phase 1 acquisition lead only: no raster payload or pixel observations were downloaded into GreenHub. Product documentation describes annual 10 m pixels, 100 km tiles, a 0.25 ha minimum mapping unit, and a confidence layer. Official CLMS announcement confirms 2022–2023 mowing datasets were released on 2025-12-02; the EEA metadata record exposes older WMS layers, so exact available years/files must be checked at acquisition. Satellite detections are not roadside-specific, do not measure biomass/yield or material removal, and do not prove collection/access/contracts. The minimum mapping unit may omit narrow verge strips. License is full/open/free subject to Copernicus attribution and modification notice. Reference metadata only; not a model input.

Phase 1 acquisition lead only: no raster payload or pixel observations were downloaded into GreenHub. Product documentation describes annual 10 m pixels, 100 km tiles, a 0.25 ha minimum mapping unit, four event-date bands, and DOY values with product-specific no-detection/non-herbaceous flags. Official CLMS announcement confirms 2022–2023 mowing datasets were released on 2025-12-02; the EEA metadata record exposes older WMS layers, so exact available years/files must be checked at acquisition. Satellite detections are not roadside-specific, do not measure biomass/yield or material removal, and do not prove collection/access/contracts. The minimum mapping unit may omit narrow verge strips. License is full/open/free subject to Copernicus attribution and modification notice. Reference metadata only; not a model input.
Primary experimental source. Table 4 gives mean ± SD by harvest date.

Primary experimental source. Tables 3–5 are transcribed into separate reference extracts for fresh grass proximate/ultimate properties, seasonal metal screen, and seasonal lignocellulose properties. Means ± SD; triplicates are analytical, not independent field sites. Do not transfer to GreenHub defaults or infer composition closure.

Printed p. 22 maps green/orange/red screening classes to CROW A+/A, B, and C/D visual litter-quality grades; identifies safety strip, high-use locations, plastics, stones, invasive species, chemical contamination, and tyre-wear microplastics. Qualitative guidance only; no measured contaminant levels, thresholds, route-specific rejection rate, or cleaning performance. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified.
Project plan and announced monitoring only. No measured gas yield, methane fraction, HRT, energy consumption or digestate analysis is available from this item; do not use as a runtime parameter.

Provinciaal Blad 2025 nr. 12664, permit description reports 36,000 t verge/nature mowing material and 24,000 t plant residues; summary does not state period or wet/dry basis. Public permit scope, not metered supply or plant operation.

Published 2025-11-28 but labels the campaign section as 2026. Lists 15 t paper, 95 t pot-stall material, and 600 t GKB own grass for Bokashi; the last is not identified as roadside material. Mass basis and campaign year are not unambiguous. Do not use in year-specific roadside supply totals.

Publisher abstract reports free amino acids 23, 15, and 14 mg/g dry weight for stubble, leaves, and roots. Reference-only: plant parts do not provide a whole roadside-grass mixture, and free-AA nitrogen may overlap with total-N-derived protein. No GreenHub default activated.
Report 2415 p.18 section 2.1.6 and Table 7 report mixed herbaceous biomass and broad verge yields; not pure grass, accessible collection, or a site-specific annual feed guarantee.

Report-only case evidence. Source tables and case bases are preserved in the linked extract; do not treat selected regional cases as GreenHub supply, a seasonal profile, or measured annual roadside availability.

Reported nitrogen-basis means are transcribed in the linked reference CSV. The mean BIN/(BIN+B2N+B3N+CN) ratio is used only to repartition Smit's total protein aggregate between GreenHub soluble and non-soluble model pools. This is class C for the GreenHub profile; no matched roadside grass juice/cake assay, transfer uncertainty distribution, or reuse license was identified.

Reports 117 t collected by five contractors in a 2024 summer dry-run; tonnage basis, dates, weigh tickets, moisture, composition, and contractor split are not published. Includes qualitative observations on five-day rest requirements, safety-strip differences, weather downtime, and a chopping/heating incident. Reference-only; not East Netherlands supply or model default.

Reports 120 t bermgras/maaisel collected with five partners but provides no measurement dates, reporting period, wet/dry basis, site split, or weighbridge evidence. Do not annualize or reconcile with the separate 117 t 2024 dry-run report. No DOI or explicit data reuse license identified; reference-only.

Reports more than 150 t/year collected during 'the past years' but provides no exact years, weighing records, moisture basis, collection scope, or measurement method. Secondary report; not comparable to the separate 117 t 2024 dry-run or undated 120 t first-party result. Reference-only; not a supply default.

Sampling was performed 2020-09-24 to 2020-11-16 across approximately 75 recently deposited grass lots. The report summarizes DM, ash, VEM, crude protein, ADL, visible litter, and As/Cd/Cr/Cu/Pb/Hg/Ni/Zn analyses. Its conclusions report Cd exceedances at 1 ANB, 2 DVW, 2 AWV regional-road, and 1 AWV motorway location; one DVW location exceeded both Cr and Ni; no exceedances were reported for As, Cu, Pb, Hg, or Zn. Group-level summary only; numerical concentrations and individual results are unavailable in the accessible PDF. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified. The cited Keurcompost limits are not GreenHub material specifications. Reference-only.

Section 11, p. 28 reports a 30,000 t/year mixed mowing-material input scenario and approximately 3.4 million m3/year potential biogas output. These are planning estimates, not measured flows or an operating plant result. Feed mass basis, grass/ditch split, gas reference conditions, composition and uncertainty are not stated. The report says procurement prevented continuation in 2021 and a 2022 restart was planned. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified.
Section 4.5.2 reports area in m2 across one-cut, two-cut, 20%-left-standing and sinusbeheer categories; not biomass or collected supply. No reuse license identified.

Sections on reduced mowing, road-specific mowing plans and Bermzeep. Factual management context only; exact tonnage, measurement protocol, source parcels and delivered feedstock are absent. No explicit open reuse license identified; not a seasonal biomass mass profile.

Table 1 reports mean ± SD (n=3) for TS, VS/TS, pH, TKN, TP, K, Na and TOC. Table 8 adds mean ± SD (n=3) sums of MUFA, PUFA, SFA and total FAMEs. Table 4 reports mean ± SD methane fractions (n=3). Results 3.1 reports only exact extreme specific biogas-yield means and SDs in prose; plotted intermediate values were not digitized. CC BY 4.0. Reference-only; not Dutch project feed or active default.

Table 1 reports untreated (UT) grass acetic acid as 0.09 g/kg fresh matter (n=2; no SD shown). The published measurement is class B evidence; its transfer to Dutch GreenHub roadside grass is class C only and remains replaceable by a matched assay. Do not infer other profile components or treatment responses from this single proxy.

Table 1 roadside-grass organic extractives, polymeric sugars, lignin, ash, liquor absorption and acid-neutralizing capacity; Phase 1 and 3 comparator. No row-level uncertainty or exact sample location/season. Table 1 gives % w/w while the composition section identifies dry basis in Figure 2; normalized basis is an explicit interpretation. Extractive/protein/sugar pools may overlap. CC BY 4.0. Reference-only; no GreenHub default or runtime activation.

Table 1 source-located mean ± SD observations, CC BY 4.0. Composition-table n not stated; author-calculated NFC and pdNDF are labeled. FR0 is reference-only, not roadside grass or a VARTA measurement. Crude-fat method code is preserved as printed pending verification.

Table 1 treatment means, Tukey groups and SEM transcribed from pp. 132-133. Cultivated timothy/lab press comparator only; no GreenHub calibration or default. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified.

Table 1, p. 130; Methods pp. 128–130. DOI not identified in the supplied sidecar; source-reported conditions only. Does not establish GreenHub reagent demand, protein recovery or an activated pH setpoint.

Table 2 reports 40 targeted PFAS and three control orchard-grass replicate profiles in µg/kg dry weight. GreenHub derived replicate sums are 4.595, 1.824, and 1.054 µg/kg dry (ND=0), mean 2.491; converted to wet basis using the VARTA sample DM fraction only as a class-C proxy. One greenhouse treatment/harvest; three composite subsamples are not independent field sites. Not Dutch roadside or VARTA evidence. Source article license: CC BY-NC 4.0; respect non-commercial terms.

Table 2 reports starch n=100, mean 34 g/kg DM, range 1–169, R²=0.77, SEC=1.45, and SEV=2.23 g/kg DM. Individual source measurements are not supplied in the table. Used only as a low-transferability class-C proxy for the GreenHub roadside/VARTA profile, not a same-sample assay. Range is not a confidence interval or probability distribution; transfer uncertainty is unquantified. Article is CC BY 4.0.

Table 27, printed p. 91 / PDF p. 92; discussion printed pp. 89–90. Mixed measurement/extrapolation/estimate; do not treat as a direct weighbridge measurement, GreenHub supply, or seasonal process input. No explicit open reuse license identified.

Table 36, printed p. 79 / PDF p. 80; notes printed pp. 78–79. Official reported inventory estimate; scope, measurement basis and collection eligibility remain as stated in the source extract. Not Dutch or GreenHub supply; reference-only.

Table 3; printed p. 17 / dissertation PDF p. 28. Concentration denominator is not explicitly labelled in the table; censored Cd/Pb and unreported four-cut S/Si remain missing/censored, not zero. Comparator only; no Dutch transfer or runtime activation.

Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5; PDF pp. 5–7; document version 2.0. Reference-only characterization; sites, seasons and protocols are not a Dutch seasonal mean or GreenHub route calibration. No explicit reuse license identified.

Tables 1, 3–5; Journal of Applied Ecology 35(3), pp. 349–364. Fitted field-retention values are not raw time series and field lying is not ensiling/storage. Reference-only; no storage runtime activation.

Tables 1–4; 2021 article. Preserve per-harvest and annual bases separately; cultivated Danish fen forage is a comparator, not roadside supply or GreenHub equipment calibration. No runtime/default activation.

Tables 2–4 report marginal means for WSC, crude protein and WSC:CP ratio across cultivar, N rate, harvest-time and cut groups. Four-replication split-plot study; no SD/SE in the tables and no joint factor-level records. B-tier source measurements; reference-only and not GreenHub roadside-grass defaults. Open access CC BY 4.0.
Tables 3 and 5; Results §§3.1 and 3.4. Distinguish field/harvest observations from theoretical supply scenarios; UK comparator only, no GreenHub supply activation.

Tables 9–11 and 23 (PDF pp. 31–32, 61–62) report mapped verge area, fresh/dry technical potential, harvest-period split, and approximate current ecological-mowing collection. The 2-cut cases are modeled future scenarios, not current contracts. Table 23 uses 33% DM. Stable report URL; no DOI or explicit reuse license identified. Reference-only.

The article identifies mapping quantity and quality as the first step of a planned pilot. No inventory values, sampling frame, dates, or analysis results are published. Acquisition lead only; not measured supply or composition.

The linked report is dated by its repository path 2021-12; its inventory estimates and mass bases are distinct and unresolved in the source package. Context-only, not direct roadside-grass measurement or a runtime supply input.

The paper reports Phleum starch as 1.88% DM but attributes it to Chornolata et al. (2018); its own Table 1 does not measure starch. The cited primary work is Chornolata, Horbachuk & Liakhovchenko (2018), Carbohydrate fractions in the green mass of forage crops, Feeds and Feed Production 85, 132–137 (in Ukrainian), https://fri-journal.com/index.php/journal/issue/view/5. Primary full text, methods, DOI and sampling uncertainty remain unverified. Use only as a low-transferability literature proxy.
Used only for explicit process statements; no unsupported defaults.

WFS schema and attribute-only extraction of 37,188 features; grouped selected berm, grass-paving and sightline records by source type, maintenance-frequency label and mowing descriptor. Source polygon-area and slope-corrected-area totals are in roadside_grass_pzh_inventory_2026_summary_reference.csv with query and aggregation provenance. Not harvested feed data: area is not grass-only, accessible, mowable or contracted supply.

Year-specific and mean yields with SD, treatment methods, and selected methane/gross-energy results transcribed from pp. 855–857. Separate proceedings source from the later 2016 journal article; press-fluid methane yield differs (269 versus the later journal's 292 L_N/kg VS maximum) and is not reconciled. Reference-only; no reuse license identified.

Zenodo version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15349657; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15349656. CC BY 4.0. Exact Zenodo Biomass.csv and Analysis.R are now vendored in the linked source folder. The 120 records are plot-level standing-biomass observations, not annual harvested or delivered supply. Reference-only; no runtime/default activation.

provenance.measurement_basis: Fresh pasture grass was cut to 2–3 cm and stored at −15 °C. Alkaline and aqueous extraction used a 1:10 solid/liquid ratio, 40 °C and 120 min; alkaline treatment used 0.1 M NaOH and pH >11, aqueous extraction used water at pH 7. Subcritical water extraction used a semi-continuous reactor at 200 °C, 40 bar, 6 mL/min for 20 min. All protein-rich aqueous extracts were adjusted to pH 3.0 using 1 M TCA, centrifuged at 13,500 × g and 4 °C for 20 min, frozen and lyophilized.
